description: Example architecture declaration for arch-drift. Models a Laravel fulfillment service that materializes orders from an upstream commerce platform. Names and vendors are illustrative.

invariants.rule: Only the ingest boundary may create FulfillmentOrder rows.
invariants.rationale: FulfillmentOrder is a local projection of an upstream order. Ingest is the one legitimate materialization point. A second creation path means rows exist here with no upstream counterpart, and the two systems then disagree about which orders are real.

except.reason: Ingest boundary implementations are the designated legitimate write path.

invariants.known_gap: Lexical. A two-line construct-then-save ($m = new FulfillmentOrder(); ... $m->save();) split across statements evades the pattern list. Needs call-site context to catch reliably.
invariants.pending_verification: Confirm against real creation sites that ingest is genuinely the sole legitimate writer before treating the except list as correct.

invariants.rule: Search resolves against local data only. The abstraction layer is fine; a remote engine is not.
invariants.rationale: An external index becomes a second source of truth that diverges silently. Divergence surfaces as items that appear searchable but cannot be picked, which is expensive to diagnose because both systems individually look healthy.
invariants.known_gap: Reads the committed config file as text. A driver set only through a runtime environment variable is invisible to a lexical check. The allowlist shape is deliberate: acceptable local drivers are enumerable, external vendors are not.

invariants.rule: Every migration is reversible while data is still disposable, or explicitly marked as an accepted exception to that rule.
invariants.rationale: Pre-production schema churn is cheap only because it can be undone. That stops being true the day real data exists, so the flexibility and the reversibility requirement expire together. Some migrations are genuinely, deliberately irreversible (a destructive backfill, a data merge with no inverse) — that's a legitimate call an author can make, but it has to be made explicitly, in the migration itself, not inferred from an empty down() that could equally be an oversight.
invariants.known_gap: Brace-matched text extraction, not parsed. A down() method that is syntactically present but semantically incomplete passes. The escape_marker is trusted on presence only: a down() carrying the '@architecturally-irreversible' comment but not actually irreversible would pass silently. That's a deliberate trust boundary — the marker is a place for a human to put a claim on record, not something this check can verify — not an oversight.

invariants.rule: External-system failures log and continue. They never block or corrupt the core workflow.
invariants.rationale: A partner being unreachable should slow the operation, not fail it. Converting a partner outage into an unhandled exception turns someone else's downtime into ours.
invariants.known_gap: Proves a handler is present, not that it degrades correctly. A catch block that rethrows satisfies this check. ->throw() is flagged separately because it is the most common way an integration silently converts a partner hiccup into a hard failure while looking unremarkable in review.

exemptions.reason: One-off backfill written before the ingest boundary existed. Slated for deletion, not migration.

Partner portal client is unauthenticated and unhardened during active build-out. Explicitly not a production-ready state. Deliberately left expired in this example (valid_through: local, a phase already behind the current pre-production phase) to demonstrate the EXPIRED path in sample output, rather than leaving it dormant until a real phase transition.

knowledge.claim: order_number is a human-readable display value. Lookups and joins use upstream_order_id, which is the upstream system's identifier.
knowledge.rationale: The display value looks enough like a key that it gets used as one. It is not guaranteed unique across upstream tenants and its format has changed before. Every bug from this class looks like a data problem rather than a code problem.
knowledge.known_gap: Proximity heuristic over a character window. A legitimate display lookup inside a search-by-reference feature will match. Expected to produce false positives; those are the point of the drift log, not a reason to narrow the window.

knowledge.claim: The carton catalog is owned upstream. This service mirrors it read-only and never writes carton definitions.
knowledge.rationale: Both systems can plausibly claim ownership of box dimensions. Leaving the direction of truth ambiguous means two catalogs drift and cartonization picks a box that does not physically exist.

knowledge.claim: 'cart' means a physical wheeled picking cart in warehouse contexts and a pre-transaction item container in commerce contexts. The two concepts are unrelated and share no schema.
knowledge.rationale: The collision is invisible in conversation and in code review. Conflating them produces logic that compiles, reads sensibly, and is wrong.

knowledge.claim: The upstream platform's 'wave' may not mean what 'wave' means here.
knowledge.rationale: Borrowed terminology is trusted only as far as it has been confirmed to exist and mean the same thing downstream. This has not been confirmed and must not become load-bearing until it is.
